briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-002
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- warehouse roof: (100, 71), roof
- water tower top: (61, 150), roof
- control room: (118, -91), indoor
- pump house: (50, -113), indoor
- water tank: (-124, 80), outdoor
- south yard: (-95, -6), outdoor
- fuel depot: (-134, -134), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 10 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2760 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 28 kg), camera. Endurance: 4920 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 10 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 2460 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1440 s, including the return to its start.
- D2 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1500 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Inspect warehouse roof with a camera. Location: warehouse roof. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T2: Deliver the spare pump (1 kg) to water tank. Location: water tank. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 1 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 120 s.
- T3: Deliver the first-aid kit (3 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 3 kg).
- T4: Inspect warehouse roof with a camera. Location: warehouse roof. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T5: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at fuel depot and keep it on board. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 120 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).
- T6: Deliver the spare pump (4 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 4 kg).
- T7: Deliver the replacement filter (3 kg) to fuel depot. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 3 kg).
- T8: Photograph control room for the condition report. Location: control room. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 420 s.
- T9: Tighten the valve at control room. Location: control room. Duration: 150 s. Needs: robotic arm. Can start only after T3 is finished.
- T10: Collect a soil sample (3 kg) at fuel depot and keep it on board. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 120 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 3 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 480 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Morning! Plan for today's site work:

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: warehouse roof (100, 71, a rooftop); water tower top (61, 150, a rooftop); control room (118, -91, indoors); pump house (50, -113, indoors); water tank (-124, 80, outside); south yard (-95, -6, outside); fuel depot (-134, -134, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 10 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 46 minutes including getting back. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 28 kg at 2 m/s and runs for 82 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 10 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 41 minutes including getting back. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 7 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 24 minutes including the flight home. D2, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera, cruises at 8 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 25 minutes of flight time, return trip included.

Jobs:
(T1) Get eyes on warehouse roof and check the panels - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T2) Water tank needs the spare pump, which weighs 1 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 2 minutes.
(T3) Control room needs the first-aid kit, which weighs 3 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T4) Get eyes on warehouse roof and check the panels - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T5) Pick up a soil sample at fuel depot and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T6) Fuel depot needs the spare pump, which weighs 4 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T7) Drop the replacement filter off at fuel depot; it weighs 3 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T8) We need pictures of control room for the report - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 7 minutes.
(T9) Someone has to tighten the valve at control room - that takes 2.5 minutes on site but only once the first-aid kit (T3) has arrived.
(T10) Pick up a soil sample at fuel depot and keep it on board; it weighs 3 kg - that takes 2 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 8 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
